'''Peter Brent Littlewood,''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Peter Littlewood |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/peter-littlewood-11826/ |access-date=4 December 2023 |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref> (18 May 1955 – 15 June 2026) was a British physicist and academic who was Professor of Physics at the [[University of Chicago]]. He was the 12th Director of [[Argonne National Laboratory]]. He previously headed the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] as well as the [[Theory of Condensed Matter]] group and the Theoretical Physics Research department at [[Bell Laboratories]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/people/littlewoodp.php |title=Professor Peter Littlewood |publisher=University of Cambridge |access-date=22 December 2013 |archive-date=24 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224090819/http://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/people/littlewoodp.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1063/1.1554133| title = Mesoscopic texture in manganites| journal = Physics Today| volume = 56| issue = 1| pages = 25–30| year = 2003| last1 = Mathur | first1 = N. | authorlink1 = Neil D. Mathur| last2 = Littlewood | first2 = P.| authorlink2 = Peter Littlewood |bibcode = 2003PhT....56a..25M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/nmat1108| pmid = 15085858| title = Nanotechnology: The third way| journal = Nature Materials| volume = 3| issue = 4| pages = 207–9| year = 2004| last1 = Mathur | first1 = N. | authorlink1 = Neil D. Mathur| last2 = Littlewood | first2 = P.| authorlink2 = Peter Littlewood |bibcode = 2004NatMa...3..207M | s2cid = 34783620}}</ref> Littlewood served as the founding chair of the board of trustees of the [[Faraday Institution]] from 2018 to 2024.

==Life and career==
Littlewood was born on 18 May 1955.<ref name=deb>{{cite web |url=http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/l/20121/Peter%20Brent+LITTLEWOOD.aspx |title=Prof Peter Littlewood |publisher=Debrett's |access-date=23 December 2013}}</ref> He gained a first-class degree in [[Natural Sciences Tripos|Natural Sciences]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1976, and was then awarded a [[Kennedy Scholarship]] to work at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for two years.<ref name=cv/> Littlewood returned to Cambridge in 1977 to complete his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web |url=http://www.santafe.edu/media/staff_cvs/PBL-CVlong.pdf |title=Peter B. Littlewood |publisher=Santa Fe Institute |access-date=22 December 2013 |archive-date=30 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130114617/http://santafe.edu/media/staff_cvs/PBL-CVlong.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Beginning in 1980, he worked at [[Bell Labs]], finishing his time there as head of the theoretical physics research after assuming the position in 1992.<ref name=cv/><ref name=news>{{cite news |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/article/2011/05/17/peter-littlewood-named-associate-laboratory-director-argonne |title=Peter Littlewood named associate laboratory director at Argonne |last=Sagoff |first=Jason |date=17 May 2011 |publisher=The University of Chicago |access-date=22 December 2013}}</ref> He continued to be a member of technical staff until 2001.<ref name=cv/>

In 1997, he became a professor at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] in Cambridge, and was head of the [[Theory of Condensed Matter group]], and served as Matthias Scholar at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] during a 2003-04 sabbatical.<ref name=news/> In 2005, he returned to Cambridge to become head of the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], before being named in 2011 the Associate Laboratory Director for Physical Sciences and Engineering at the [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name=news/>  On 25 March 2014, Littlewood was named to the director's post.  In January 2017, he retired as director to resume his research at the University of Chicago.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.politico.com/tipsheets/morning-energy/2016/11/greens-regroup-for-unexpected-battle-217555 |title = Greens regroup for unexpected battle|website = [[Politico]]| date=23 November 2016 }}</ref> Since 2022, he also held a partial appointment at the [[School of Physics and Astronomy, University of St Andrews|School of Physics and Astronomy]] of the [[University of St Andrews]] in Scotland, UK.
Peter Littlewood held various advisory roles at Faraday Institute <ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.faraday.ac.uk/the-faraday-institution-announces-inaugural-board-of-trustees/ |title=Chair of the Board of Trustees of Faraday Institute, UK}}</ref> and Flatiron Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/people/peter-b-littlewood/ |title=Scientific Advisory Board, Flatiron Institute, USA}}</ref>

Littlewood held six [[patent]]s, published more than 200 articles in [[scientific journal]]s and gave more than 200 invited talks at international conferences, universities and laboratories.<ref name=news/>

Littlewood died in Chicago on 15 June 2026, aged 71.<ref>[https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2026/06/18/remembering-physicist-and-emeritus-trustee-peter-littlewood/ Remembering Physicist and Emeritus Trustee Peter Littlewood]</ref>

==Honours and positions==
From his [[curriculum vitae]], 2010.<ref name=cv/>
* Member, National Academy of Sciences, 2025
* Fellow, Royal Society of London, 2007
* Fellow, Institute of Physics, 2005
* Matthias Scholar, Los Alamos National Laboratory, 2003-2004
* Consultant, Los Alamos National Laboratory, 2004-
* Consultant, National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, 2004-
* Fellow, Trinity College Cambridge, 1997
* Fellow, American Physical Society, 1989
* Distinguished Member of Technical Staff, AT&T Bell Laboratories, 1989
* Professeur Associé and visiting scientist, CNRS, Grenoble, 1986
* Denman Baynes Student, Clare College, Cambridge 1979-80
* Kennedy Scholar, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, 1976–77
* Senior Scholar, Trinity College Cambridge, 1974–76

==Work==
Littlewood's research variously included studying the phenomenology and microscopic theory of high-temperature [[superconductors]], [[transition metal oxides]] and other correlated electronic systems, and the optical properties of highly excited semiconductors. He applied his methods to engineering, including [[holographic storage]], optical fibers and devices, and new materials for particle detectors.<ref name=cv/><ref name=news/> 

Littlewood was also involved in research related to [[magnetic 2D materials]].<ref> [https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/09/260929053548.htm Electrons slow to a crawl in a strange new quantum state]</ref>
